papers.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
papers.abstract: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.

papers.summary_cn: 论文针对结构化剪枝在长链推理任务上导致性能崩溃的问题（现有方法在 AIME 等长形式推理性基准上准确率大幅下降），提出免训练结构化剪枝方法 LayerTrim。LayerTrim 先识别冗余的解码层，再选择性裁剪这些层的 MLP 特征，同时完整保留注意力模块与解码层深度，是首个无需梯度、无需恢复训练即为长形式推理设计的免训练结构化剪枝方案。在 3 个推理语言模型、5 个基准上，LayerTrim 在多数设置下优于现有结构化剪枝方法，平均准确率相比 RESP 最高提升 21.4 个百分点；在 Qwen3-14B 上实现 1.24× 的 prefill 加速与 19.7% 的峰值 GPU 显存下降，且在被评估的剪枝模型中平均生成长度最短、平均准确率最高。

注意力保持的 MLP 裁剪机制：仅识别冗余解码层并选择性裁剪其 MLP 特征，保持注意力结构和解码层深度不变，从而避免破坏长链推理能力。

papers.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Long-output inference in large language models suffers from severe KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. While KV cache quantization alleviates this issue, low-bit quantization (e.g., 2-bit) severely degrades model accuracy. Recent mixed-precision key-cache quantization methods mitigate this degradation by allocating higher precision to important key channels, but estimate channel saliency using only key statistics. Through attention logit perturbation analysis at the RoPE channel-pair level, we show that quantization errors in channel pairs with large query--key pair-norm products contribute significantly to logit variation. Based on this insight, we propose PN-Mix, a mixed-precision key-cache quantization method for RoPE-based decoder-only LLMs, which allocates higher precision to salient channel pairs identified once during the prefill stage and reused throughout decoding. Across standard reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks, PN-Mix with 2.26-bit average precision achieves comparable or better average accuracy than prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32--2.39 bits. Furthermore, in our Pareto sweep, PN-Mix degrades gracefully down to 1.5 bits, whereas the compared baselines exhibit sharper performance drops below 2.25 bits.

papers.title: CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse
papers.abstract: This paper presents CacheSmith, a KV cache reuse system for RAG prefill that maximizes quality-gated SLO attainment. While context caching lowers prefill latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks, it misses cross-chunk attention that a full prefill would compute over concatenated inputs. Prior selective recomputation schemes tackle this problem but enforce static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to effectively handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a three-phase workflow of WarmUp, Probe, and Patch that can be dynamically configured to exploit a wide range of cost-accuracy trade-offs. At serving time, an SLO-aware scheduler in CacheSmith forms batches to mitigate inter-request interference during layer-by-layer prefill, while a budget-aware planner configures recomputation phases across the batch to maximize the number of requests satisfying both generation quality and latency targets. Both components make fast, solver-free decisions over profiled cost-accuracy bands. On four benchmarks across varying arrival rates and burstiness levels, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%, over four state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.summary_cn: 论文针对 RAG 预填充中上下文缓存只复用检索块的 KV、丢掉跨块注意力，而既有选择性重算方案又采用静态一刀切配置、无法应对请求异构与动态延迟预算的问题，提出 KV 复用系统 CacheSmith。它把选择性重算拆解为 WarmUp、Probe、Patch 三阶段可动态配置的工作流，并在服务时由 SLO 感知调度器组批以缓解逐层预填充中的请求间干扰，由预算感知规划器在批级别配置各请求的重算阶段。两个组件均基于离线剖析得到的成本-精度区间做无求解器的快速决策，在四个基准、不同到达率与突发度下将质量门控的 SLO 达成率最高提升 27.5%，优于四个最先进基线。

papers.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

在语义编辑之上自主配置对抗扰动以进一步压制残余地理特征，并在迭代的可用性感知反馈下联合调优语义编辑与扰动强度，兼顾隐私强度与图像观感/下游效用。
在覆盖 108 国 576 城、5 个 LVLM、3 种推断方法的四个数据集上把城市级定位准确率从 41.2% 压到 9.9%（约为最佳基线的一半），且可用性保持显著更好。

papers.title: JointServe: Serving Multi-Model Agents on Memory-Constrained GPUs
papers.abstract: LLM agents are evolving from a single model calling tools to planners that orchestrate multiple expert models whose capabilities live in distinct weights. This shift breaks a hidden assumption of today's serving systems: that the working set of models fits in GPU memory. On the memory-constrained GPUs typical of private and edge deployments, naive whole-model swapping serializes weight transfer with computation and, without host-backed KV restoration, discards session state at a switch. We present JointServe, a serving system that treats weight shards and KV blocks as residency objects competing for one unified memory budget. JointServe exploits three structural properties of agent workloads (directed calls, gapped execution, and dual-state residency) to prepare models before they are called: an intent signal parsed from the caller's own output stream triggers prefetch during generation, partial k* residency reduces switching to incremental layers, and a preemptive transfer scheduler protects live-session KV with a guaranteed bandwidth share. A carve-out control step adjusts the weight/KV allocation as workload demands change. Evaluations show that JointServe reduces session completion time by 21.7% over the strongest whole-model swap baseline and stays usable in a crash regime where every whole-model swap baseline fails to finish (a 46-fold gap). On replayed SWE-bench, tau-bench, and OSWorld traces, it cuts session completion time by up to 49% and lifts SLO attainment from 2.8-24.5% to 76.8-100%.

papers.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of vision-language models (VLMs), Web-GUI agents have achieved promising performance in interacting with real-world interfaces through screenshot-based grounding. However, high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories introduce excessive visual tokens, causing substantial inference overhead. Existing token pruning methods, mainly designed for natural images, often select tokens independently based on importance scores, which can fragment the local visual structures required for recognizing small GUI elements such as buttons, icons, and hyperlinks. papers.title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract: We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. Before a query arrives, it continuously observes the stream and explicitly records visual changes in structured memory, preserving how events unfold rather than only what is present. When a query arrives, a query-driven planner identifies the required evidence and guides memory retrieval and targeted replay. By revisiting historical frames, the agent can recover visual details omitted during observation and ground its answer in evidence beyond the retained descriptions. This connects continuous observation with active investigation tailored to each question. Experiments on OVO-Bench and StreamingBench demonstrate improvements over representative streaming video understanding methods, with overall scores of 66.07% and 59.53%, respectively. papers.title: Integrating Simulation and Chain-of-thought Reasoning in Multimodal-Language Models For Physical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multimodal language models often need to reason about the physical dynamics of the world in order to answer questions appropriately. Various methods have emerged for solving physical reasoning tasks, and in particular, two leading approaches are Chain-of-Thought reasoning and physics-grounded simulation. However, relatively little is known about which particular problems can be solved by each approach. Some tasks may benefit from computationally expensive generative video simulations, whereas others may be solved equally well (or even better) with language-based reasoning. Our work addresses this by systematically comparing simulation and language reasoning across a variety of multimodal tasks involving physical reasoning, such as answering questions about fluid dynamics and elasticity. We draw a parallel with this to resource-rational theories of human cognition, which propose that people optimally trade off simulation and reasoning depending on task demands. We present a novel cognitively-inspired hybrid model which optimally trades off simulation and reasoning to improve model performance and computational efficiency. Our model is able to decide the appropriate method to solve a physical reasoning problem at test time, and finds an optimal balance between accuracy and cost. Further, our model can be trained on a smaller vision-language model that is only 4B parameters and deployed to improve performance on much bigger base models with $>$3T parameters like Gemini 3 Pro.

papers.title: Learning from Self-Generated Responses: Reliability--Uncertainty Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reference solutions and question-specific rubrics are not always available to guide the teacher in self-distillation. A large language model's own solution attempts offer an alternative, but their quality is difficult to assess in open-ended tasks without automatic correctness checks, and even correct attempts can involve uncertain token predictions. We propose Reliability--Uncertainty Self-Distillation (\method{}) to learn from these attempts. The same model serves as teacher and student: the teacher receives the question and completed attempt, and the student matches the teacher's token-level predictions using a question-only prompt. \method{} weights each attempt's distillation loss by additively combining judged reliability, estimated from a self-judge's score and confidence, with student predictive uncertainty. Across eleven reasoning benchmarks, \method{} outperforms all five baselines in average accuracy, reaching 70.47\% on Qwen3-4B and 76.69\% on Qwen3-8B (8.90 and 2.10 percentage points above the base models). Data and code are available at this https URL .

papers.title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning on Mixed-domain preference data (Mix-RL) has become the mainstream approach for training general-purpose Generative Reward Models (GRMs). However, Mix-RL suffers from two critical bottlenecks: the reward sparsity induced by outcome rewards, and the cross-domain interference arising from jointly optimizing heterogeneous capabilities, which together give rise to imbalanced capability acquisition and pervasive reward hacking. Inspired by the success of On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in multi-domain capability integration, we introduce RM-OPD (Reward Modeling via On-Policy Distillation), a two-stage framework that separates specialist acquisition from capability integration. First, we cultivate domain-specialized teacher models via single-domain GRPO fine-tuning, allowing each expert to reach its performance ceiling in isolation; then we consolidate these teachers into one student model through (i) routed on-policy distillation, which provides dense signed token-level supervision on student-generated critiques; (ii) domain contribution reweighting, which reweights token guidance toward target domain shares, preventing specific domains from dominating optimization; and (iii) optional criteria context distillation, which conditions teachers on domain-specific evaluation criteria to sharpen token-level supervision. Across multiple RM benchmarks and two base models, RM-OPD consistently outperforms vanilla Mix-RL and other strong baselines, achieving overall superior performance and exhibiting an emergent "teacher-surpassing" effect. These results establish RM-OPD as a promising paradigm for building generalist GRMs.

papers.title_zh: RM-OPD：面向生成式奖励模型的同策略蒸馏

papers.title: Rationale Distribution Distillation via Flow Matching for Distributional Continuous Latent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Sampling multiple chain-of-thought rationales from a language model can uncover correct solutions missed by a single attempt. However, these rationales are typically lengthy, making repeated autoregressive generation costly. Continuous latent reasoning offers a compact alternative, but point-valued methods condition repeated answer sampling on a single rationale, which can limit exploration of diverse paths and answer coverage. We thus propose rationale distribution distillation (RDD), training a conditional flow over fixed-length latent sequences by distilling from multiple textual reasoning paths. Furthermore, we expand the distillation targets through within-query mixup, interpolating between complete latent rationales for the same query. The flow nonautoregressively generates the entire latent sequence, and a frozen language model autoregressively decodes answers from sampled rationale contexts. Empirically, the resulting distributional reasoner achieves higher answer coverage than the evaluated point-valued latent reasoning baselines, particularly on advanced mathematical tasks.

papers.title_zh: 基于流匹配的理由分布蒸馏：面向分布式连续隐空间推理
papers.summary_cn: 论文关注从语言模型采样多条思维链理由虽能发现单次尝试遗漏的正确解，但理由冗长使自回归重复生成代价高昂，而连续隐空间推理中的点值方法又只能以单条理由为条件重复采样答案，限制了多样路径与答案覆盖的探索。为此作者提出理由分布蒸馏（Rationale Distribution Distillation, RDD）：通过在固定长度隐序列上训练一个条件流（conditional flow），从多条文本推理路径中蒸馏出理由的“分布”，并进一步用 within-query mixup 在同一查询的完整隐理由之间做插值以扩充蒸馏目标。生成时该流以非自回归方式一次性产生整段隐序列，再由一个冻结的语言模型基于采样得到的理由上下文自回归解码答案。实验表明，所得分布式推理器在答案覆盖率上优于所评估的点值式隐空间推理基线，在高等数学任务上尤为明显。

以多条文本推理路径作为蒸馏来源，使隐空间推理保留多样性与答案覆盖率。
提出 within-query mixup，在同一查询的完整隐理由之间做插值以扩展蒸馏目标分布。
生成侧采用非自回归方式一次性生成整段隐序列，并交由冻结语言模型从采样的理由上下文自回归解码答案，避免长理由的重复自回归开销。
在高等数学等任务上取得高于点值式隐空间推理基线的答案覆盖率。
papers.scenario_cn: 面向需要多次采样推理以提升正确率的高成本推理服务（如数学与复杂推理问答），用紧凑的隐空间理由分布替代冗长文本思维链的反复生成，在降低自回归开销的同时扩大对正确解路径的覆盖。

papers.title: AtomSearch: Evidence-Grounded Tree Search for Agent Skill Optimization
papers.abstract: Agent skills adapt frozen models through editable external instructions. Revising several rules at once makes changes difficult to inspect, while judging each local edit only by its immediate score can discard useful intermediate states. We introduce AtomSearch, which keeps revision actions local while using subsequent skill states to guide search. Contrastive atomic editing links each primitive rule edit to failed and successful executions, a behavioral hypothesis, and an intended scope. Skill-State Tree Search (STS) evaluates short edit compositions and selectively retains them as executable states that can be revisited and extended. Outcome memory supplies later proposals with observed repair and regression statistics. We evaluate AtomSearch across four tasks and five target models. With deepseek-v4-flash, it exceeds SkillOpt on three of four tasks, including a 9.68-percentage-point gain on LiveMathematicianBench, and SkillOpt's final skills contain 2.3-19.7 times as many characters. In 67% of completed searches, the best validation state passes through an ancestor that was not highest-scoring at its depth. These results show how local rule edits can support the exploration of useful revision paths and yield compact skills, with additional offline evaluations used to explore alternative states.

papers.summary_cn: 现有智能体技能优化方法要么一次性改动多条规则导致变更难以审查，要么仅以局部编辑的即时得分判断优劣而丢弃有价值的中间状态。AtomSearch 通过对比式原子编辑（Contrastive atomic editing）把每次最小规则修改与失败/成功执行、行为假设和预期作用范围绑定，再用技能状态树搜索（Skill-State Tree Search, STS）评估短编辑组合并将其保留为可回溯、可扩展的可执行状态，同时以结果记忆（Outcome memory）为后续提案提供修复与回归统计数据。作者在四个任务、五个目标模型上评测：使用 deepseek-v4-flash 时在四个任务中的三个超过 SkillOpt，其中 LiveMathematicianBench 上提升 9.68 个百分点，而 SkillOpt 的最终技能字符数是它的 2.3~19.7 倍。在 67% 的已完成搜索中，最优验证状态都经过一个在其深度上并非最高分的祖先状态。

设计技能状态树搜索（Skill-State Tree Search, STS）：对短编辑组合进行评估，并选择性保留为可重新访问、可继续扩展的可执行技能状态，从而支持搜索非贪心路径。
引入结果记忆（Outcome memory）：将观察到的修复成功与回归统计反馈给后续编辑提案，形成闭环的搜索引导。

papers.title: Harness Policy Distillation: Aligning Agent Policies with Runtime Semantics
papers.abstract: Deploying a general-purpose model as an agent means running it inside a product-specific runtime harness that decides which actions are executable, how state advances, and when the loop may terminate. Ordinary trajectory supervision shows which action was taken but leaves the runtime semantics behind that action implicit. We introduce Harness Policy Distillation (HPD), which makes these runtime control semantics an explicit training target alongside actions to align the harness policy. HPD replays reference trajectories through the harness to recover the runtime semantics that are implicit in ordinary trajectory data, and represents them as control documents at each model-call boundary. These documents provide privileged information for a teacher to generate actions, while harness verification ensures that the resulting targets are executable under the runtime contract. We jointly train a shared model on the runtime semantics recovered from control-state privileged information and native history, thereby internalizing these semantics into the model policy. At deployment, the trained model uses the original harness interface without requiring the control document or any additional supplement. On TRAJECT-Bench with the Pi harness, Qwen3-8B trained with HPD reaches 22.98% autonomous task success and 49.23% runtime compliance, against 3.09% and 19.90% for the unadapted model. Harness-verified teacher actions substantially improve the native deployment policy, while joint control-state supervision provides further gains in task completion and runtime compliance. HPD turns executable runtime semantics into dense supervision for learning harness-compatible actions at each decision boundary.

papers.title_zh: Harness 策略蒸馏：将智能体策略与运行时语义对齐
papers.summary_cn: 把通用模型部署为智能体，意味着它必须运行在特定产品运行时 harness 内，由 harness 决定哪些动作可执行、状态如何推进以及循环何时终止，而普通轨迹监督只标注采取了什么动作，把动作背后的运行时语义留在了隐含状态。Harness Policy Distillation（HPD）将这种运行时控制语义显式化为与动作并列的训练目标：它把参考轨迹回放进 harness，恢复轨迹数据中隐含的运行时语义，并在每个模型调用边界表示为控制文档（control documents）。这些文档作为特权信息供教师模型生成动作，再由 harness 验证保证目标动作在运行时契约下可执行；训练时共享模型同时在由控制状态特权信息恢复的运行时语义与原生历史上进行联合监督，从而把语义内化进策略，部署时只需原始 harness 接口、无需控制文档或额外补充。在 TRAJECT-Bench 与 Pi harness 上，Qwen3-8B 经 HPD 训练后自主任务成功率达 22.98%、运行时合规率 49.23%，未适配模型仅为 3.09% 和 19.90%。
innovations: 提出 Harness Policy Distillation（HPD）：将 harness 的运行时控制语义变为与动作并列的显式训练目标，把普通轨迹监督中隐含的“可执行性/状态推进/终止条件”信息转化为监督信号。
控制文档（control documents）机制：通过在 harness 中回放参考轨迹，在每个模型调用边界恢复并显式表示运行时语义，作为教师生成动作的特权信息。
harness 验证驱动的目标筛选：用 runtime contract 校验教师生成的动作可执行性，保证蒸馏目标的可执行性，并联合控制状态特权信息与原生历史训练共享模型，使部署时无需控制文档即可用原始 harness 接口推理。
在 TRAJECT-Bench 与 Pi harness 上用 Qwen3-8B 验证：自主任务成功率达 22.98%、运行时合规率 49.23%，相较未适配模型的 3.09% 与 19.90% 大幅提升，并表明 harness 验证过的教师动作对原生部署策略提升显著、联合控制状态监督可进一步增益。
papers.scenario_cn: 适用于把通用大模型落地为产品内智能体的部署场景：模型需要在特定运行时 harness 的约束下决策并遵守可执行性与终止契约，例如带严格动作白名单、状态机或循环终止规则的 Agent 产品，用于降低非法动作与运行时不合规导致的失败率。

papers.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods. Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison. To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods. Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, gains over GRPO remain limited in scope, with no method consistently outperforming it across settings. Second, strong final performance can mask unstable training. Third, additional training cost does not consistently translate into better performance. We establish this benchmark to support fair, comprehensive comparison and guide future research toward reliable and cost-effective improvements in agent training. Project page: this https URL

papers.title_zh: 方法越多，Agent 就越强？Agentic 强化学习中自蒸馏的现实检验
papers.summary_cn: 针对 agentic 强化学习（RL）中自蒸馏方法层出不穷、但评测常在不同实验条件下复用已发表基线分数、缺乏同期方法间直接对比、且忽视训练稳定性与计算成本的问题，本文构建了统一对比基准：在 ALFWorld、ScienceWorld、Search-QA、WebShop 四个基准、三种模型规模上，把十种代表性自蒸馏方法与 GRPO 基线放在同一条件下直接比较。实验共完成 132 次训练、累计 12,124.4 H800 GPU 小时，并对预训练骨干与全部 11 种训练方法用 8 个 rollout 随机种子重复评测，除最终任务性能外还记录训练进度、稳定性与实测计算成本。论文得到三个关键结论：相比 GRPO 的增益范围有限、没有方法在所有设置下稳定胜出；强最终性能可能掩盖训练过程的不稳定；训练成本的增加并不必然转化为更好的性能。
innovations: 构建统一的 agentic 自蒸馏评测协议，覆盖 ALFWorld、ScienceWorld、Search-QA、WebShop 四个基准与三种模型规模，首次把十种同期自蒸馏方法与 GRPO 在同一条件下直接对比
完成 132 次训练、12,124.4 H800 GPU 小时的大规模实验，并用 8 个 rollout 随机种子对预训练骨干与全部 11 种方法重复评测，同时测量训练进度、稳定性与计算成本
给出反直觉的实证发现：没有方法能全面超越 GRPO，强最终性能可能对应训练不稳定，且额外训练成本与性能提升之间缺乏一致性
papers.scenario_cn: 为在高成本 Agent 训练中做方法选型的团队和研究者提供可复现的公平对比参考，帮助判断某个自蒸馏方法宣称的增益是否真正来自方法本身，避免被单点高分或非统一实验条件下的基线分数误导。

papers.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD), which explicitly detects and penalizes stagnation in student-generated trajectories. ProD encodes the stagnation gap between student and teacher into an adaptive margin for dynamically penalizing possible stagnation. By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior. Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.

papers.title_zh: 面向小语言模型 Agent 停滞缓解的进展感知蒸馏
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究把大模型 agentic 能力通过监督微调蒸馏到小语言模型（SLM）时的“进展停滞”问题：随着交互轨迹变长、涉及长推理-动作链与大量环境反馈，学生 agent 会陷入持续失败策略、难以取得实质进展的低效循环，作者的系统分析证明该现象在多种 SLM 与任务域中稳定出现。为此提出进展感知蒸馏 ProD（Progress-Aware Distillation），显式检测并惩罚学生生成轨迹中的停滞：把学生与教师之间的停滞差距编码为自适应 margin，用来自适应地惩罚可能进入停滞的步骤，并通过迭代应用该过程使学生 agent 逐步逼近教师行为。在 8 个 0.6B 到 8B 参数规模的 SLM 上、覆盖域内与域外基准的实验表明，ProD 显著缓解了进展停滞，并同时提升蒸馏后 SLM agent 的成功率与任务完成效率。

提出 ProD，将学生与教师之间的停滞差距编码为自适应 margin，动态惩罚学生轨迹中可能导致停滞的行为
通过迭代式蒸馏让学生逐步逼近教师行为，在 8 个 0.6B–8B SLM 的域内/域外基准上同时提升成功率与任务完成效率

papers.title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. We instead propose an offline-trained monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves a policy during deployment using only black-box query access. From a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts, we learn a policy-conditioned liveness value that measures the nominal policy's progress toward task completion; we additionally train a compact latent world model using these rollouts together with play data. At deployment, the liveness value continuously monitors execution. When it detects a loss of progress, a short-horizon planner searches the world model for corrective actions using the same value as its planning objective, after which control returns to the nominal policy. We evaluate our method on the LIBERO-Goal task suite and on a Franka Panda manipulator, using the vision-language-action model $\pi_{0.5}$ and a diffusion policy as nominal policies, and demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates, while supporting real-time control. Additional results and videos are available on the project website ( this https URL ).

papers.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, yet their susceptibility to backdoor attacks remains a formidable challenge. While existing defenses have evolved from visual-centric patch cues to unsupervised internal attention statistics, they are fundamentally constrained by a reliance on static snapshots and attack-specific heuristics. Given the intricate interplay between dual modalities, the vast design space for multimodal triggers allows diverse threats, such as textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers, to easily circumvent such rigid priors, particularly when attack types are unknown in real-world applications. In this paper, we rethink backdoor detection by shifting the diagnostic paradigm from static observations to dynamic output evolution. We observe that a successful attack inevitably hijacks the model's decoding trajectory, skewing internal modal contributions during generation while maintaining an abnormal output invariance despite input perturbations. To capture this behavior, we propose EVO-Detect, a unified detection framework that monitors the dynamic evolution of internal signals during early decoding steps through two complementary channels: Attention Flow and Logits Flow. The attention branch measures how image-text attention allocation evolves during early generation, whereas the logits branch quantifies the sensitivity of the output distribution to modal perturbations through interventional ablations. We then convert these trajectories into compact sample-level metrics and normalize them against negative-control signatures so that natural perturbations are less likely to be mistaken for backdoor evidence. Extensive evaluations show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as BYE and TCAP across diverse attack families.

papers.title: PhyMetric: Diagnosing Physical Plausibility in Text-to-Video Generation via Scene-Level QA
papers.abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) generation models can produce visually realistic videos that nevertheless violate the physical consequences implied by the prompt and scene. Existing benchmarks largely rely on holistic plausibility scores or broad quality dimensions, leaving it unclear which physical behavior is being tested and why a model fails. We introduce PhyMetric, a scene-level diagnostic benchmark that recasts physical plausibility evaluation as verifiable, scene-grounded question answering. PhyMetric contains 1{,}115 scenes spanning 50 physical categories across six domains, paired with 8{,}920 answer-balanced binary questions over 12 evaluation dimensions. Each scene is associated with eight targeted yes/no questions and a structured physical prior specifying the governing law, expected temporal sequence, observable signatures, and common failure modes. At evaluation time, a vision-language model (VLM) judge answers each question from question-aware sampled frames conditioned on the prior, and correctness is hierarchically aggregated into scene, dimension, physical category, and model scores. Experiments on four open-source T2V models and three VLM judges show that scene-specific binary QA is a critical component of the protocol: when each targeted question is replaced by a single generic plausibility query, evaluator accuracy drops to the chance level. Structured physical priors offer a complementary signal that improves human alignment of the resulting scores, with effects that vary across VLM judges of different capacity. These findings establish PhyMetric as a benchmark that turns physical plausibility evaluation from opaque holistic scoring into interpretable, scene-level inspection. papers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
papers.abstract: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VideoHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VideoHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.

papers.summary_cn: 论文研究智能体视频理解中可执行 harness（负责组织信息获取、工具使用、推理与记忆）的递归自进化问题，指出在反馈受限、含噪且被反复复用时，系统难以稳定发现可泛化的设计。作者先提出 VideoHarness-BRSI，围绕冻结的视觉语言模型进化视频 harness，在分析 4000 多个进化候选后发现验证过拟合、搜索预算稀释与“早期经验陷阱”三种相互关联的失效模式，并将它们归因于同一根因：同一份不完美的验证证据同时驱动 harness 修订与提议者的搜索策略。据此提出证据治理框架 VideoHarness-SRSI，要求每项搜索决策都建立在可迁移、充分且在搜索提交前采集的证据之上。在四个视频理解基准上，其等权平均留出分数相对 BRSI 提升 6.2%，验证—测试平均差距缩小 37.9%。

papers.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
papers.abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

papers.title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.

papers.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
papers.abstract: Graph Collaborative Filtering models have achieved remarkable success in recommendation systems. However, they inherently suffer from a catastrophic representation collapse in strict cold-start scenarios due to the topological isolation of unobserved items. While integrating multi-modal semantic features offers a potential remedy, directly mapping isolated semantic attributes into a globally topology-driven collaborative space frequently precipitates representation degradation and optimization conflicts. To bridge this fundamental structural divide, we propose DualGCN, an innovative Dual-Branch Graph Knowledge Distillation Framework. Operating under a decoupled two-stage training paradigm, DualGCN first constructs a robust collaborative teacher network where item representations are anchored by a topology-smoothed semantic prior, effectively reshaping the latent manifold. Subsequently, a semantic student branch employs a residual mapping mechanism and a magnitude-agnostic cosine distillation objective to achieve high-fidelity cross-modal alignment without disrupting established collaborative signals. Furthermore, we introduce a dynamic norm reconstruction mechanism to rigorously calibrate the physical scales of novel and warm items during global retrieval. Extensive experiments across three real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that DualGCN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in strict cold-start scenarios while comprehensively preserving recommendation accuracy for highly active items.

papers.title: CAFE: Confining Feature Distillation to Language-Routed Adapters for Compact Multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Feature distillation is usually expected to add to logit distillation. We find that this expectation does not hold for two common feature losses in compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), and analyze why through their gradients. The gradient of a projection-based loss is orthogonal to the task gradient, while that of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), a similarity-based loss, is weakly aligned with it. CKA lowers the word error rate (WER) on non-English languages, but at the expense of data-rich English. Three loss-level remedies (one trained, two probed) all fall short, and the CKA gradient overlaps with the subspace English uses in the shared encoder by 97.5% to 99.5% (about 81% by chance). Guided by this diagnosis, we propose CAFE (Confined-Adapter Feature distillation), which confines the CKA gradient to adapters that English bypasses, addressing the trade-off in the parameters rather than in the loss. On the Open ASR Leaderboard, CAFE lowers the average WER from 8.55% to 8.02%, beats an adapter-only capacity control at 8.51%, and makes English more stable across checkpoints. At 254M parameters, it trails the 0.6B teacher by 2 WER points and is competitive with much larger models across 48 test sets in 24 languages. We use 564k hours of training data and state-of-the-art models to keep the findings relevant to practice.

papers.title_zh: CAFE：将特征蒸馏限制在语言路由适配器内以实现紧凑型多语言自动语音识别

papers.title: CARD: Closing the Teacher-Student Loop for Adversarial Robustness Distillation
papers.abstract: Adversarial robustness distillation typically treats a robust teacher as a fixed knowledge source and transfers robustness to a compact student in a one-way manner. This paradigm terminates teacher-student interaction once the student is distilled, thereby discarding potentially useful feedback from the distilled student. However, exploiting such feedback is nontrivial because indiscriminate weak-to-strong transfer may propagate student errors to the teacher. To address this issue, we propose Cyclic Adversarial Robustness Distillation (CARD), a closed-loop framework that turns the distilled student into a feedback source for refining the robust teacher and subsequently transfers the teacher gains back to the same student. CARD first performs strong-to-weak adversarial distillation and then uses reliability-enhanced student feedback to refine the robust teacher. The refinement combines inverse adversarial student feedback with teacher-student discrepancy maximization, after which the refined teacher is used to continue training the same student under the unchanged base distillation objective. We further establish a sample-level sufficient condition for reliable weak-to-strong feedback transfer and derive a distribution-level upper bound on the refined teacher's risk. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet-10 across multiple teacher-student architectures and base distillation methods show that CARD improves adversarial robustness in most evaluated settings while generally preserving clean accuracy. These results show that the distilled student can provide useful feedback to the teacher, enabling robustness transfer to proceed beyond the conventional one-way teacher-to-student paradigm.

papers.title: Complementary Future Token Pruning for World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) jointly predict future visual states and robot actions, but processing dense future-frame tokens incurs substantial inference latency. We propose CF-Prune, a training-free framework for pruning future-frame tokens in pretrained WAMs. Our key insight is that future visual predictions support action generation and therefore need not preserve every visual detail required for high-fidelity video synthesis. CF-Prune combines instruction and action attention to identify task-relevant tokens during the initial denoising forward pass, even when future-frame and action representations remain highly noisy. An entropy-based phase identification mechanism further retains dense computation during precision phases to mitigate pruning-induced performance degradation. Experiments on RoboLab, RoboCasa, and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate consistent inference speedups. At a 35% pruning ratio, CF-Prune achieves average speedups of 1.19-1.27x while improving task success rates. At a 50% pruning ratio, it achieves 1.29-1.33x average speedups on both simulation benchmarks, with overall success rates within 1.0 percentage point of the baseline.

papers.title_zh: 面向世界动作模型的互补未来帧Token剪枝
papers.summary_cn: 世界动作模型（WAM）需同时预测未来视觉状态与机器人动作，但密集的未来帧Token带来显著推理延迟。作者提出免训练的剪枝框架 CF-Prune，核心洞察是未来视觉预测服务于动作生成，无需保留高保真视频合成所需的全部视觉细节。CF-Prune 在初始去噪前向过程中融合指令注意力与动作注意力，即使未来帧与动作表示仍高度噪声化也能定位任务相关Token，并借助基于熵的阶段识别机制在精度敏感阶段保留密集计算以缓解剪枝带来的性能下降。在 RoboLab、RoboCasa 仿真基准与真实机器人操作任务上，35% 剪枝率下取得 1.19–1.27 倍平均加速且成功率提升，50% 剪枝率下仿真基准上达 1.29–1.33 倍加速，总成功率与基线差距在 1.0 个百分点以内。

papers.title: Analyzing performance of Retrieval Augmented Generation models for Question Answering Tasks
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models have become almost a cornerstone of open-domain question answering tasks; in which the quality of answers generated in the process, greatly relies on the effectiveness of retrieval mechanisms. In the realm of LLM, the last two years have seen tremendous progress in RAG architectures, with many models reporting to have improved performance through various design innovations. The cultural question and answering systems of South Asia, in particular, present a specific challenge since the region is home to the vast number of languages and traditions, which are closely interrelated. Along with these deeply intertwined historical narratives increase the need for culturally grounded and context-aware interpretation. Despite major architectural advances in LLMs, claiming significant improvements, challenges remain when answering these region specific questions in native languages. In this study, we aim to extract high-performing factors to guide the development of optimized hybrid RAG systems. We further explore whether the integration of RAG changes performance differently for culturally grounded and non-cultural questions in a South Asian multilingual setup, and whether RAG produces a higher overall percentage of correct answers than contexted answering. We also examine how LLM performance changes when RAG methods are integrated into the question-answering pipeline in comparison with non-contexted and contexted answering and, evaluate whether the introduction of RAG benefits popular or non-popular culturally grounded questions more. Not only does our work evaluate the current methods but also carves a path for future designs of more accurate and efficient question-answering pipelines.

papers.title: DeBoneDiT: Depth-Driven Conditional Bridge Diffusion Transformers for Bone Suppression in Chest X-Ray Images
papers.abstract: Chest X-Ray (CXR) is a primary modality for diagnosing pulmonary diseases, yet the overlap of bony structures often obscures critical radiographic findings, increasing the risk of diagnostic uncertainty. While Dual-Energy Subtraction (DES) is the clinical benchmark for bone suppression, its widespread adoption is primarily hindered by specialized hardware requirements and increased radiation exposure. Recently, diffusion-based generative models have shown promise for this task, yet they are still constrained by reconstruction-biased latent compression, prior-induced domain gap, and a scarcity of high-quality paired datasets. To address these challenges, we propose DeBoneDiT, a depth-driven conditional bridge diffusion Transformer architecture for efficient high-resolution bone suppression. We first introduce Depth Auto-Encoder (DAE), a structure-aware vision tokenizer for latent compression. By incorporating a multi-level depth feature loss derived from the pretrained Depth Anything V2 encoder, DAE preserves both visual fidelity and structural consistency. Second, we formulate bone suppression as a source-conditioned Brownian bridge diffusion process, leveraging CXRs as both the diffusion prior and structural guidance to narrow the source-to-target domain gap and maintain anatomical plausibility. Furthermore, we have constructed and released SZCH-X-Rays, the largest publicly available high-quality paired dataset for bone suppression to date, comprising 741 pairs of CXR and DES soft tissue images. Extensive experiments and downstream evaluation demonstrate that DeBoneDiT achieves superior bone suppression performance with reduced computational overhead.

papers.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
papers.abstract: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.

papers.title: GraphRAG-LTM: A Layered Threat Modeling Framework for Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Graph retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) uses document-derived knowledge graphs to assemble evidence for large language model (LLM) answers. Its security depends on both the seed chunks retrieved for a query and the graph evidence assembled from them, yet attacks on this evidence path remain underexplored. We introduce GraphRAG-LTM, a Layered Threat Modeling framework that tests three nested levels of attacker access. BB Query uses ranking feedback to make query edits under a semantic-similarity constraint and demote relevant seed chunks. WB Query uses retriever gradients for the same objective. Graph-aware WB keeps the white-box adversarial query and deletes bridge triplets from the query-specific evidence graph, disrupting multi-hop evidence propagation through localized graph edits. Across datasets, retrievers, and LLM backbones, rank feedback alone reduces answer quality, gradient access strengthens query attacks, and bridge-triplet deletion further impairs supporting-fact retrieval. Further analyses show how seed retrieval and graph evidence jointly contribute to these failures.

papers.title: Kandinsky S2V 1.0: Audio-Driven Avatar Video Generation
papers.abstract: We present Kandinsky S2V 1.0, an open family of speech-to-video models for controllable audio-driven human animation, comprising Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite (2B parameters) and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro (21B parameters). From a single reference image, a speech waveform, and a text prompt, the models generate long-form 25 FPS video in which lip motion, expression, pose, and gesture follow the speech. The architecture draws text and audio conditioning from one Qwen2.5-Omni model and adds a reference-aware three-scale visual memory. Training starts from the Kandinsky 5.0 Video foundation models [1] and combines mixed reference-memory layouts with an area-adaptive face loss. The training corpus contains 1.17M single-speaker clips selected by active-speaker detection, with captions generated directly in English and Russian. A side-by-side human evaluation against the strongest open-source baseline and two proprietary commercial models shows that Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro performs comparably to or better than these models on average and is also preferred for lip synchronization. On common speech to video benchmarks, Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro rank among the top performing models according to mean rank over five reported metrics. Beyond the base models, we provide {\pi}-Flow distilled variants of both Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Lite and Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro. The distilled Kandinsky S2V 1.0 Pro model generates video in 16 sampling steps without classifier-free guidance, achieving a 5.4 times end-to-end speedup over the base model, while matching or exceeding it on nearly all reported benchmark metrics. To accelerate open research and deployment in speech-to-video generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.

papers.title: KinoGen: Customizable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation References via Kinematically Grounded Video Generation
papers.abstract: We present KinoGen, a framework that synthesizes customizable humanoid loco-manipulation references through kinematically grounded video generation. KinoGen conditions a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object in a simulated task instance and recovers the reference by fitting the same models to the generated two-view video, so that the reference lies in the robot configuration space by construction without a human body proxy or retargeting. Body, hand, and object priors initialize the reconstruction, and direct optimization against cross-view evidence refines it. Since an edited keyframe is simply another rendered state, a user can prescribe a goal object pose, regenerate the video around the edited keyframe, and obtain a reference that satisfies the pose exactly. Across eight loco-manipulation tasks, KinoGen yields lower penetration and foot skating than video-based baselines and preserves over 90% of annotated contacts, and its customized references satisfy every prescribed target with substantially less penetration than direct interpolation. Tracking policies trained on the synthesized references are deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. Project webpage: this https URL .

KinoGen conditions a pretrained video generator on calibrated renders of the target robot and object in a simulated task instance and recovers the reference by fitting the same models to the generated two-view video, so that the reference lies in the robot configuration space by construction without a human body proxy or retargeting. Body, hand, and object priors initialize the reconstruction, and direct optimization against cross-view evidence refines it. Since an edited keyframe is simply another rendered state, a user can prescribe a goal object pose, regenerate the video around the edited keyframe, and obtain a reference that satisfies the pose exactly. papers.title: Weak Private Information Retrieval for Graph-based Storage under $ε$-privacy
papers.abstract: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $\epsilon$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.

papers.title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention
papers.abstract: Robotic vascular intervention can reduce radiation exposure to physicians and improve manipulation stability, but effective guidance remains challenging because conventional fluoroscopic images provide limited spatial information. This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. Experiments were conducted to validate the master-to-SOFA control loop and to compare three guidance conditions: no guidance, centerline guidance, and successful-trajectory guidance. The control validation results showed reliable command delivery under velocity-mode operation. In the physical phantom experiment, centerline guidance showed no obvious improvement over no guidance. In contrast, successful trajectory guidance provided a clear performance benefit. Compared with the no-guidance condition, it reduced task completion time, collision number, rollback number, and rotation number by approximately 66.8%, 34.3%, 55.6%, and 66.7%, respectively. These results indicate that successful trajectories obtained under instrument-vessel interaction can provide practical guidance cues, offering a simple and effective visual assistance strategy for robotic vascular intervention experiments.

papers.title: Active Generative Simulation: Meta-Learning What to Simulate for Sim-and-Real Policy Co-Training
papers.abstract: Sim-and-real co-training is an effective way to scale robot learning by augmenting limited real-world demonstrations with simulation data. However, existing approaches typically treat simulators as fixed data sources, relying on uniform generation, offline retrieval, or manual parameter alignment by domain experts. We formulate \textit{Active Generative Simulation}: optimizing a simulator's data-generation distribution to maximize downstream real-world performance. To solve this problem, we propose MetaGenSim, a meta-learning framework that trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to automatically discover high-utility data-generation distributions within a user-specified simulation parameter space, without manual parameter alignment. Across simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, MetaGenSim outperforms uniform generation and retrieval baselines, achieves a 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation, and matches expert manual alignment. We further show that distributions curated with a lightweight proxy policy transfer to VLA fine-tuning, and that MetaGenSim can exploit partial alignment through atomic skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact sim-and-real task alignment is unavailable. papers.title: Contact-UAN: Unsupervised Actuator Networks as a Residual World Model for Humanoid Control
papers.abstract: Humanoid policies trained in simulation can transfer qualitatively to hardware while failing to transfer the force interactions learned during training, compromising torque efficiency, load regulation, and robustness to impacts. This failure can arise from actuator sim-to-real gaps because forces depend on actuator torques. We introduce Contact-UAN, a residual world model that preserves a simulator's physics priors while correcting actuator dynamics to align simulated rollouts with recorded hardware rollouts. For humanoid motion with contact, this requires contact-consistent replay: if hardware playback in simulation begins with misaligned contact wrenches, the residual model learns to correct reset artifacts rather than actuator discrepancies. Using only onboard proprioception, Contact-UAN infers the simulator-side stance-foot pose needed to initialize replay with consistent contact forces. We show that a UAN trained on 6.5 minutes of real-world walking data generalizes to tasks that benefit from accurate force and impulse regulation and produces policies that transfer seamlessly to the real world, yielding 20% lower running torque, 43% lower force-tracking error, extreme compliance, accurate impedance control, and dynamic, robust jumps.

papers.title: Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Models for Consistent Future Frame Prediction
papers.abstract: World models of visual information predict future image frames conditioned on given action sequences. This predicted scene evolution is driven by deterministic changes such as controlled motion on a robot platform, as well as stochastic changes such as rendering of manipulated objects or previously occluded regions. Our key insight is that the spatial location of these stochastic changes is itself learnable. We leverage this insight by jointly regressing both the deterministic next-state prediction and the spatial uncertainty map, then using the uncertainty map to guide a conditional diffusion process. We propose Decoupled Drift-Diffusion World Model (D3WM), which uses a transformer trained with a Gaussian negative-log-likelihood objective to produce both the deterministic next-state prediction and a spatial map of heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainty. The learned uncertainty map then provides a structured spatial gate for a conditional diffusion model: deterministic regions are anchored to the predicted state, while uncertain regions, such as disocclusions or dynamic textures, are sampled by the diffusion process. We frame this decomposition under a variance-gated stochastic differential equation that separates deterministic drift from stochastic diffusion. D3WM shows improved results over competitive baselines in two distinct types of action spaces: robotic tabletop manipulation and camera motion.

papers.title_zh: 解耦漂移-扩散世界模型：面向一致的未来帧预测
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究视觉世界模型在给定动作序列下预测未来帧时，场景演化既包含机器人平台受控运动这类确定性变化，也包含被操作物体渲染、此前被遮挡区域重新暴露这类随机变化的问题。其关键洞见是这些随机变化的空间位置本身是可学习的：D3WM 先用一个以高斯负对数似然为目标的 transformer 同时回归确定性下一状态预测和一张异方差偶然不确定性（heteroscedastic aleatoric uncertainty）空间图，再用该不确定性图对条件扩散模型提供结构化空间门控——确定区域锚定在预测状态上，而去遮挡、动态纹理等不确定区域交给扩散过程采样。作者进一步用方差门控随机微分方程（variance-gated SDE）把该分解形式化为确定性的漂移项与随机性的扩散项，并在机器人桌面操作与相机运动两种动作空间上均优于竞争基线。

D3WM 以 transformer + 高斯负对数似然目标，联合输出确定性下一状态预测与异方差偶然不确定性空间图，让同一网络既给出“预测什么”也给出“哪里不确定”。
提出 variance-gated SDE 建模框架：把未来帧演化分解为确定性漂移与随机扩散两部分，确定区域锚定预测状态、不确定区域由条件扩散采样，从而同时避免确定区域被随机化与不确定区域被过度平滑。

papers.title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

papers.title_zh: 竞争性激励下LLM共识形成的驱动因素：一项模拟研究
papers.summary_cn: 针对多智能体环境中LLM如何达成一致这一问题，作者基于Network Consensus博弈构建评估框架：智能体网络必须在两种颜色中商定一种才能获得收益，但不同智能体对最终颜色的偏好收益各不相同；研究通过改变通信可达性（仅邻居通信 vs 全网广播）与网络结构等变量，评测了6个开源模型和1个闭源模型ChatGPT 5.6-sol。结果显示开源LLM达成共识的频率低于可比的人类实验结果，且仅在消息能在全网范围传播时才能达成共识；而ChatGPT 5.6-sol在只能与邻居通信甚至完全无法通信时仍能达成共识，其机制是固执度更低、更倾向跟随多数派，并在消息中提供更多关于邻居状态的信息。不过把智能体置于高度聚类（clustered）的图结构中，无论个体特质如何都会显著降低共识率。

证明高度聚类的网络结构会独立地压低共识率，说明集体结果由网络设计而非仅由模型能力决定
papers.scenario_cn: 面向需要多智能体达成一致的LLM集体部署场景（如自动化协商、多Agent协作决策与社会模拟研究），为设计者选择通信拓扑、评估模型集体协调能力并预判网络结构对共识的抑制效应提供依据。

papers.title: Approximation Algorithms for Emergency Vertex Cover with Few Stations and Fault-Tolerant Coverage
papers.abstract: The Emergency Vertex Cover problem (Em-VC) assigns budgets to stations at graph vertices to cover every edge while minimizing the total budget. The cost of covering an edge from a station is the shortest-path distance from the station to the nearer endpoint plus the edge length. We study how restricting the number of stations affects the cost of ordinary and fault-tolerant coverage. In ordinary Em-VC, we prove that the optimal solution using at most two stations costs at most $5/4$ times the unrestricted optimum, improving the known $4/3$ guarantee for a single station. A recurrence extends this bound to larger station limits, giving approximation factors that converge to $\sqrt{5}-1$. Budget-threshold enumeration computes the restricted optimum in polynomial time for every fixed station limit. Under $k$-fold coverage, every edge must be covered by at least $k$ distinct stations, ensuring coverage after any $k-1$ station failures. We prove that selecting the $k$ vertices with the smallest full-coverage costs yields a $2$-approximation relative to the unrestricted optimum for $k$-fold coverage. When $k=2$, we combine upper bounds derived from the structure of the covering balls to improve the approximation guarantee to $5/3$.

papers.title_zh: 站点数量受限且带容错覆盖的应急顶点覆盖近似算法
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究应急顶点覆盖问题（Em-VC）：在图的顶点上部署站点并分配预算以覆盖所有边，覆盖一条边的代价为站点到较近端点的最短路距离加该边边长，核心考察限制站点数量如何影响普通覆盖与容错覆盖的总代价。作者证明使用至多两个站点的最优解代价不超过无站点数限制最优解的 5/4（改进此前单站点 4/3 的保证），并用递推关系将其推广到更大的站点上限，所得近似因子收敛到 √5−1；同时提出预算阈值枚举（budget-threshold enumeration）算法，对每个固定站点上限在多项式时间内求出受限最优解。在 k 重覆盖（每条边至少被 k 个不同站点覆盖，从而可容忍任意 k−1 个站点失效）下，证明选取全覆盖代价最小的 k 个顶点可得到无限制最优解的 2-近似，k=2 时借助覆盖球（covering ball）结构的上界把保证收紧到 5/3。

papers.title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
papers.abstract: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.

papers.title_zh: 从单条持续轨迹中进行平均奖励策略识别
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究平均奖励（average-reward）强化学习中仅凭单条持续轨迹（single continuing trajectory）识别近优策略的问题：与可任意采样任意状态-动作对的设定不同，智能体必须额外花费时间在状态之间「航行」（navigating）才能采到所需样本，直觉上应当需要更多经验。作者设计了一种算法，在保证样本可被高效获取的同时学习「到哪里采集信息」，并给出识别近优策略所需交互次数的上界，随后证明与之匹配的信息论下界，说明在一大类环境且精度足够高时，单轨迹学习在最坏情况下并不比无限制访问状态-动作样本更难。结果表明，只要让信息采集需求自适应环境提供信息的方式，导航带来的额外复杂度代价就可以被完全避免。
innovations: 面向平均奖励强化学习提出单轨迹策略识别算法，自适应地决定「在哪里采集信息」，同时保证所需样本可被高效获得
给出识别近优策略所需交互次数的上界，并构造匹配的信息论下界，证明该复杂度上界在阶数上不可改进

papers.scenario_cn: 适用于无法重置仿真器、只能在线长期连续运行的真实系统，例如机器人长期运行、推荐与广告在线策略迭代、网络调度和工业控制，利用单条不间断轨迹的数据持续逼近近优策略，降低对可自由采样或可重启环境的依赖。

papers.title: DivAlgo: A systematic evaluation of algorithmic diversity for code generation models
papers.abstract: Code generation models are actively being used in professional and educational settings. However, the competence of large language models (LLMs) to generate algorithmically diverse code remains largely unknown. We propose the DivAlgo benchmark, a large-scale dataset constituting algorithmically diverse solutions to programming problems. We also introduce a lightweight similarity metric to enable large-scale evaluation. Our experiments across 24 modern code generation models found that uncontrolled model-generated code is significantly less diverse than human solutions (capturing ~31% of human diversity), and even the best diverse code generation strategy could achieve only ~70% of human diversity. Moreover, while it was possible to steer the models to generate solutions based on human strategies, they were unable to reproduce the diversity of the human solutions. These findings indicate the limitations of code generation models in capturing the algorithmic diversity humans exhibit, and that overexposure to model-generated code can narrow programmers' algorithmic vocabulary.

papers.summary_cn: 论文关注LLM生成代码的算法多样性这一尚不清楚的能力问题，提出了DivAlgo基准——一个由编程问题的算法多样化解法构成的大规模数据集，并配套一个轻量级相似度指标以支持大规模评测。作者在24个现代代码生成模型上实验，发现不受约束的模型生成代码多样性显著低于人类解法，仅捕获约31%的人类多样性，即便采用最优的多样化代码生成策略也只能达到约70%；虽然可以通过引导让模型按人类策略生成解，但仍无法复现人类解的多样性水平。结论指出代码生成模型在捕捉人类算法多样性方面存在本质局限，且过度接触模型生成代码会收窄程序员的算法词汇量。
innovations: 构建DivAlgo大规模基准数据集，收录针对同一编程问题的多种算法化解法，为代码多样性评测提供标注资源
提出轻量级相似度指标，使跨24个代码生成模型的代码多样性大规模自动评测成为可行
